title: the Rust Belt Rising
premise: When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the Meridian system, cargo navigator Odile Voss and the ragtag crew of the Rust Belt Rising discover their ship's hold contains illegal neural backups of the colonists of Vantage Station—a settlement officially recorded as never having existed. The nine-second flicker was a weapon test by Consolidated Orbital, which erased Vantage and its forty thousand residents from every archive, and Odile's own missing memories are tangled in it: she was born there. Hunted by a corporate retrieval fleet and betrayed by an ally, the crew races to broadcast the backups' testimony before CO can purge the last physical evidence. In the end, Odile chooses to wake the backups rather than keep them safe in silence, sacrificing her ship's anonymity—and her chance to ever learn which of her memories are truly hers—to make the massacre undeniable, while her found family builds a new life aboard a renamed vessel carrying witnesses instead of cargo.
about_author: Beatrix Yarrow is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route manifests in the industrial Midwest before turning to science fiction. Their work explores labor, memory, and the quiet heroism of people who move things for a living.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A routine haul through contested orbits is shattered when gravity across the entire system flickers for nine seconds; instruments scream, cargo shifts, and Odile wakes screaming from a dream she can't remember. The crew discovers their sealed hold now registers forty thousand faint life-signs that shouldn't exist. Beat: dread disguised as confusion.

chapters.title: The Hold That Breathes
chapters.summary: Engineer Tam Okafor's POV. Tam pries into the hold against Odile's protests and finds racks of neural backup cores, cold-storage preserved, each labeled with names and dates—dated five years ago, the same year Odile signed on. Captain Reyes orders everything resealed. Beat: unease deepening into complicity.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cross-referencing the core labels, Odile finds her own childhood surname among them and a birthplace called Vantage Station—which every database insists was never built. She hides the discovery from the crew. Beat: identity cracking open like ice on a spring river.

chapters.title: Consolidated Courtesy
chapters.summary: Captain Ilsa Reyes's POV. A CO patrol frigate hails the Rising with suspicious politeness, requesting an 'inspection of anomalous mass signatures.' Reyes bluffs them off but knows the clock has started. First glimpse of Commander Hale, too calm, too knowing. Beat: the noose tightening politely.

chapters.title: What the Dockhands Know
chapters.summary: Deckhand Junie Park's POV. At Ceres Freeport, Junie trades contraband gossip for parts and learns other ships felt the nine-second flicker—and that three vessels who reported it have since vanished from registries. The crew votes, narrowly, to investigate rather than run. Beat: found family choosing danger together.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nothing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew tracks down Sefa Ilves, a disgraced archivist who once mapped Vantage Station's orbital slot. Sefa confirms the colony existed and was deleted—but claims the flicker wasn't a weapon. It was a signal, and something answered. Beat: wonder braided with terror.

chapters.title: Backups Don't Dream
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam interfaces with one dormant core as a diagnostic and experiences fragments of a woman's final hours: sirens, air loss, a child being loaded onto a shuttle. He realizes the cores aren't archives—they're testimony, deliberately hidden inside freighters like theirs. Beat: grief arriving secondhand.

chapters.title: Hale Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Commander Hale boards under diplomatic pretense, compliments the ship, and offers Reyes a fortune to surrender 'misdelivered property.' Reyes refuses; Hale leaves a tracker they only half-successfully disable. Beat: corruption wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Girl on the Shuttle
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cross-checking the child from Tam's fragment against her own fragmented memories, Odile confronts the possibility she was evacuated from Vantage at age six, her past scrubbed by whoever smuggled her out. She finally tells the crew everything. Beat: shame transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. With CO patrols sweeping the lanes, the Rising goes dark, drifting cold through a debris field while hunters pass close enough to hear hull creak. Junie keeps the youngest crew member calm with invented card games. Beat: terror held at bay by tenderness.

chapters.title: Sefa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa reveals she kept a physical index of Vantage records hidden in a dead relay station—but demands passage off-system and immunity in exchange. En route, the crew discovers Sefa once sold data to CO, fracturing trust. Beat: alliance strained over old wounds.

chapters.title: The Relay at the End of the Map
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The salvage of the relay station goes wrong when a CO trap springs; Tam takes shrapnel saving the index, and Junie barely pulls him home. They have the records, but the Rising is bleeding air and credibility. Beat: sacrifice proving family is chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Decoded, the index proves Vantage's deletion was systematic—forty thousand identities unwritten by executive order. But proof means nothing without distribution, and every broadcast node in the system is CO-controlled. Beat: triumph curdling into despair.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Sefa, terrified, secretly contacts CO offering the cores in exchange for amnesty. Junie catches the transmission and must decide whether to expose her or give her a chance to confess. Sefa confesses, weeping; the crew locks her quarters but doesn't space her. Beat: mercy as a radical act.

chapters.title: What Hale Wants
chapters.summary: Hale's POV (interlude). Through Hale we see CO's logic: the flicker was a memory-weapon calibration, Vantage its test bed, and the backups the loose thread that could unravel a technology worth trillions. Hale is offered command if she closes the case. Beat: banality of evil, humanized just enough to chill.

chapters.title: Wake Them or Bury Them
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew debates: waking the backups lets them testify but exposes them to capture or worse; keeping them dormant preserves lives but not justice. Odile argues for waking them—the dead deserve voices. The vote passes. Beat: moral climax of principle over safety.

chapters.title: Forty Thousand Witnesses
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, braided. The first cores wake in shifts: farmers, teachers, a dockworker who recognizes the Rising's old registry. Their testimony floods the ship's memory banks. One elder recognizes Odile's face. Beat: awe, grief, and the weight of being believed.

chapters.title: The Battle of Broken Orbit
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. CO corners the crippled Rising above Vantage's erased coordinates. Outgunned, the crew uses the nine-second gravity flicker's residual signature—now understood—as a decoy pulse, scattering the patrol long enough to bolt for the deep-space array. Tam, wounded, pilots the escape. Beat: desperate, costly victory.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the ancient array, they transmit everything: records, testimony, the weapon's signature. CO jams the primary channels, so the awakened colonists themselves speak, voice after voice, until jamming becomes censorship too visible to hide. Hale receives stand-down orders as the story goes system-wide. Beat: catharsis through collective voice.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Ordered to destroy the Rising and take the blame, Hale instead surrenders her fleet logs to the tribunal, choosing ruin over complicity. Sefa testifies about her betrayal and is granted leniency for turning witness. Beat: accountability as imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Which Memories Are Mine
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Offered restoration of her original memories via the cores, Odile declines—not out of fear, but because she chooses the self her found family helped build. She visits the memorial being raised at Vantage's coordinates and reads her parents' names aloud. Beat: identity as something made, not recovered.

chapters.title: Cargo No Longer
chapters.summary: Full-crew ensemble. The Rising, refitted and renamed the Forty Thousand, signs its first contract: ferrying returning colonists and witnesses to rebuild what was erased. Odile takes the navigator's chair, the hold empty and full of light. Final line echoes the opening dream—this time, no one wakes screaming. Beat: hopeful resolution, found family sailing forward.
